pron.heading: Pronunciation tip
pron.final: At the end of a word or before a consonant, a final consonant that is a tense or aspirated stop, s, j or ch (k-, t-, p-types and sibilants) is pronounced as plain k, t or p, for example {ex}.
pron.liaison: When a single or double final consonant is followed by a particle, ending or suffix that starts with a vowel (written with a silent initial consonant), the final consonant is pronounced as the start of the next syllable, for example {ex}.
pron.nasal: A final stop sound (k, t or p type) becomes a nasal sound (ng, n or m) before a nasal consonant (n or m), for example {ex}.
pron.lateral: When an n sound and an l/r sound meet across a syllable border, they are usually pronounced as l (there are a few exceptions), for example {ex}.
pron.tense: After a final stop sound (k, t or p type), the next plain consonant (g, d, b, s or j type) is pronounced tense, for example {ex}.
pron.source: Source: Standard Pronunciation Rules of Korean, article {art} (National Institute of Korean Language).
pron.note: This tip explains a rule. Your device voice only plays sound; this app does not judge your own pronunciation.
modes.title: Choose a review mode
modes.intro: Review the same material in different ways. Only questions from stages you have already reached appear.
modes.choice.desc: Pick the correct answer from the options.
modes.listening.desc: Listen to a sentence and choose the same one from the options.
modes.order.desc: Arrange the word pieces in the right order. A different natural word order can also be correct.
modes.dictation.desc: Type the sentence you hear exactly. Spelling must be correct; in English, capital letters and extra spaces or punctuation are forgiven. Korean word spacing is not forgiven.
modes.noSound: If you cannot hear sound, review with “Choose from options” or “Put in order”. Sound settings and help are on your profile.
modes.cards.desc: See the front of a word, recall its meaning, then check the back. This does not affect your XP, level or review schedule.

tts.title: Voice and sound settings
tts.voice.none: No {lang} voice is installed on this device.
tts.disclaimer: The device voice only reads the text aloud. It does not check your own pronunciation.
tts.help.title: No sound, or no {lang} voice?
tts.help.check.volume: Turn the media volume up and, on an iPhone, switch off silent mode.
tts.help.check.mute: Make sure the browser tab is not muted and that sound is not going to a Bluetooth speaker you are not using.
tts.help.check.browser: Browsers inside other apps may not speak. Open this page in the phone's normal browser (Safari, Chrome, Edge).
tts.help.ios: iPhone / iPad: Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Voices, choose {lang} and download a voice.
tts.help.android: Android: Settings → Language & input (or General management) → Text-to-speech → voice data, and install {lang}.
tts.help.windows: Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech (or Language & region) and add the {lang} language pack and voice.
tts.help.mac: Mac: System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → System Voice → Manage Voices, and add a {lang} voice.
tts.help.restart: After installing, close the browser completely and open it again: the voice then appears in the list.
tts.help.menus: Menu names differ a little between devices and versions.
tts.help.alt: You can still practise without a voice: solve from the text and the romanization, or start with the questions that need no sound.
